moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Perform advanced editing on tests using keyboard shortcuts, or by passing information into a test step through parameters.
Demonstrate the process of copying values directly from the web or mobile application to be used in later test steps.
Synchronize tests with application behavior by waiting for specific events like element visibility, text display, or file downloads.

elements.description: Sends a specified keyboard shortcut combination (e.g. Ctrl+C) to the AUT during execution — added like other predefined Actions. It's cross-platform by design: a shortcut recorded on Windows (e.g. Ctrl+C) is automatically translated to its Mac equivalent (Cmd+C) at execution time, and vice versa.

In the step's Properties panel, under the Keyboard Shortcut section, placing the cursor in the Windows field and pressing the keys (all at once) auto-fills the equivalent in the Mac field — or the reverse, starting from the Mac field. Whichever platform the test actually runs on at execution time, Testim uses the corresponding field.

Not every possible key combination is supported. If you use a keyboard shortcut Testim doesn't recognize, it presents an 'unsupported keyboard shortcut' error rather than silently ignoring it, defaulting to something else, or blocking the whole test from running.

bulletPoints: Add Keyboard Shortcut step sends a key combo to the AUT — an Actions-menu predefined step.
Cross-platform by default: Windows ↔ Mac shortcut translation happens automatically based on the Properties panel fields.
An unrecognized combination throws an explicit 'unsupported keyboard shortcut' error.

elements.description: Parameters let a step or group be customized per use — passing in different information without knowing every value in advance — so the same underlying steps serve multiple scenarios instead of being copy-pasted with small edits each time.

When both parameters and test data could supply a value for the same field, parameters take precedence over test data. Within Testim's layered override system specifically, config-file parameters override params-file parameters, and — within the config file — a beforeTest hook's values override a beforeSuite hook's values; params-file parameters, in turn, override the default test data/run data.

bulletPoints: Parameters pass custom information into a step/group instead of hardcoding it.
Precedence: parameters generally override test data — and within parameter sources, config-file > params-file > default test data, with beforeTest overriding beforeSuite inside the config file.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Extract Value: capturing data for later steps

elements.description: The Extract Mode of an Extract Value step determines the value and format of the contents captured into an extract variable — for example, pulling an order number or a generated OTP code off the page and storing it so a later step can use or validate it. Selecting the mode is done directly in the step's own Properties, not through code, and not through a project-level setting.

elements.text: This is the same pattern used to grab a verification code from an email/SMS inbox: extract only the stable value you actually need (the code, a link, a subject line) rather than trying to assert on the whole message body.

bulletPoints: Extract Value captures a value from the page (or another source) into a variable.
The data type to extract is set via the step's own Properties (Extract Mode) — not in code, and not in Project Settings.
Extract only the specific, stable value you need — not the entire surrounding content.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Wait for Events: synchronizing tests with the application

elements.term: Waiting for an event, not a fixed time
elements.description: Testim can wait for a specific event to occur before proceeding to the next step — an element becoming visible, specific text appearing, or a file finishing its download — rather than a plain, guessed time delay. This is the same condition-based-waiting principle covered for basic Wait For steps, applied to a broader set of real application events.

elements.term: Wait for element visible / not visible
elements.description: Wait for element visible pauses until a target element appears; Wait for element not visible pauses until an element disappears (e.g. a loading spinner clearing). Both are added the same way as other predefined steps: hover the arrow, open Testim's predefined steps, pick the step, then select the target element.

elements.term: Changing the element after the fact
elements.description: If the wrong element was targeted (or the element changed), the fix is the same as for any other step's target element: open the step's Properties and use Reassign to point it at a different element — not deleting and re-recording the step, and not just adjusting the wait duration (which doesn't fix a wrong target).

bulletPoints: Waitable events include element visibility, text display, and file downloads — not just a fixed duration.
Wait for element visible / not visible are added like any other predefined step, then targeted at an element.
To retarget a wait step's element, use Properties → Reassign — the same mechanism as any other step, not re-recording.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming an unrecognized keyboard shortcut fails silently or gracefully degrades
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting Testim to ignore an unsupported key combination and continue the test, or to substitute the closest supported shortcut.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: An unsupported combination produces an explicit 'unsupported keyboard shortcut' error — it doesn't get ignored, silently substituted, or merely block the run without explanation.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming test data always wins over parameters
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Defining both a parameter and matching test data for the same field and expecting the test data value to be used.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Parameters take precedence over test data. Within the parameter sources themselves, config-file values override params-file values, which in turn override the default test data.

examPitfalls.title: Re-recording a Wait for element visible step just to point it at a different element
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Deleting and re-recording a wait step from scratch because the wrong element was targeted.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Open the step's Properties and use Reassign to point it at the correct element — the same target-element mechanism used on any other step, no re-recording required.

examPitfalls.title: Extracting an entire block of text instead of the specific value needed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Capturing a whole confirmation message or email body with Extract Value, then trying to parse it in a later step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure the Extract Mode to capture only the specific, stable value needed (an order number, an OTP code) so later steps can use it directly without extra parsing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does Testim react if you use a keyboard shortcut that it does not recognize?

options.text: Testim will show an error saying unsupported keyboard shortcut.
Testim defaults to the closest equivalent keyboard shortcut.
Testim will add the keyboard shortcut step to the test case but will not let you run the test.
Testim will ignore the unrecognized keyboard shortcut and continue the test execution.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's an explicit, named error — not a silent fallback.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Unsupported key combinations present the explicit error 'unsupported keyboard shortcut' — Testim doesn't substitute a similar shortcut, silently skip it and continue, or add-but-block-running the step.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What happens when both parameters and test data are defined for a test step?

options.text: Parameters always take precedence over test data.
Test data always overrides parameters.
Parameters can override test data based on usage.
Both are ignored, and default values are used.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about the override chain: config-file > params-file > default test data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Parameters take precedence over test data. This holds within Testim's layered override system too: config-file parameters override params-file parameters, which in turn override the default test data/run data.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can a user select the type of data to be extracted from a web page while using a extract value step?

options.text: The user can enter the extract value step properties and set the extract mode.
The user can specify the data type when writing the code for the step.
The user can navigate to the Project Settings panel and set the required data type.
The user can only extract strings using the extract value step.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a per-step setting, not a project-wide or code-based one.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The data type to extract is controlled by the Extract Mode property, set directly in that step's own Properties — not by writing code, not in Project Settings, and Extract Mode supports more than just plain strings (number, date, regex-matched text).

practiceQuiz.scenario: What should you do if you want to change the element after selecting the "Wait for element visible" option in Testim?

options.text: Go to the "Properties" menu and reassign a different element.
Delete the current step and re-record it with the new element.
Change the wait duration to allow more time for the element to appear.
Access the main menu and choose a different wait option.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same target-element mechanism used everywhere else in Testim.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Retargeting a wait step's element uses the same mechanism as any other step: open Properties and use Reassign. Deleting and re-recording is unnecessary, adjusting the wait duration doesn't change WHICH element is targeted, and there's no separate 'main menu' for this.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Besides waiting for an element to become visible, which of the following is also something Testim's Wait for Events functionality can synchronize a test against?

options.text: A file finishing its download.
The tester's mouse movement speed.
The number of open browser tabs.
The project's billing plan tier.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think application-behavior events: visibility, text, and this one.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim can wait for events like element visibility, specific text display, or a file finishing its download before proceeding — not mouse movement speed, tab count, or billing details, which aren't waitable application events at all.

quickRecap.value: Sends a key combo to the AUT; auto-translates Windows ↔ Mac; unsupported combos throw an explicit error.
Customize a step/group per use; take precedence over test data (config-file > params-file > default test data).
Per-step Properties setting controlling what data type is captured — not code, not Project Settings.
Synchronize on element visibility, text display, or file downloads — not a guessed fixed delay.
Properties → Reassign, same as any other step — no re-recording needed.
